_comment: Security headers autumn-web's middleware stamps on every origin response.
A CDN serving files from dist/ runs none of that middleware, so without
restoring them here every statically served page would carry fewer
protections than the same page from the origin. That is a security
This file is the single source of truth. Both sides read it:
tests/static_export.rs    asserts the origin emits exactly these and no
So a framework upgrade that adds a fifth header fails the test and names
the file to edit, rather than quietly shipping a weaker bundle.
content-security-policy is in the list because autumn-web's value is a
constant, not a per-request nonce. It was briefly excluded as 'volatile',
where it belongs, because a wasm capsule structurally cannot emit it. A
static bundle has no such constraint, and dropping the strongest header in
the set for a reason that does not apply is exactly what this file exists

headers.content-security-policy: default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'
